The '''Bio-antidote package''',<ref name="KOTOR" /> also called the '''Bio-antidote system''' was an [[Cybernetics/Legends|cybernetic]] implant that maintained an stream of antitoxins circulating in the user's [[Blood/Legends|blood]]. The implant would increase the levels of the relevant [[Antidote/Legends|antidotes]] when a poison was introduced into the user's body, rendering the user immune to all poison effects. The implant required an initial level of healthiness before it could be equipped, and sometimes caused dry mouth as a side effect.<ref name="KOTOR2" />

A Bio-antidote package could be created at a workbench with sufficient tools, chemicals, and skill.<ref name="KOTOR2" /> During the [[Jedi Civil War]] between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and [[Darth Revan's Sith Empire|Sith Empire]]<ref name="KOTOR" /> in [[3956 BBY]],<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> the implant was in use by the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]]. [[Zelka Forn]], a [[Doctor/Legends|doctor]] in the [[Upper City]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] [[Ecumenopolis/Legends|ecumenopolis]] of [[Taris/Legends|Taris]], owned one of these implants, which he was willing to sell for five hundred [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]].<ref name="KOTOR" /> By [[3951 BBY]], five [[Standard year/Legends|years]] later,<ref name="K2Date">''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' places the events of ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]'' in [[3956 BBY]]. In-game diogogue from ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]'' places it five [[Standard year/Legends|years]] after the events in the first game. Therefore, the sequel must take place in [[3951 BBY]]</ref> the implant was more widely accessible and could be bought from merchants throughout [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] at a price of seventy-five credits.<ref name="KOTOR2" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Bio-antidote package first appeared in the [[2003]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]'', developed by [[BioWare]].<ref name="KOTOR" /> It later appeared in the [[2004]] sequel, ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]'', developed by [[Obsidian Entertainment]].<ref name="KOTOR2" /> While the item appeared in a specific shop and specific locations throughout the first game,<ref name="KOTOR" /> the randomized inventories of merchants and loot drops of enemies mean that it has a chance to appear in several shops and locations.<ref name="KOTOR2" />

In ''Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic'', a character must have the "Implant Level 3" feat in order to equip the Bio-antidote package.<ref name="KOTOR" /> In ''Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords'', a character must have a constitution attribute of fourteen or higher to equip the item.<ref name="KOTOR2" />
